title: Buoyancy & Floating
intro: Why the sufuria floats but the nail sinks: Archimedes with jerricans, clay boats, hydrometers and lake safety.

lessons.title: Sink or Float? The Prediction Game
lessons.focus: Predict then test twenty local objects (nail, coin, maize cob, charcoal, bottle top, mango seed, stone, leaf, wax, wire); tabulate surprises.
lessons.advanced: From the class table, state the rule that beats 'heavy things sink' with three counter-examples.

lessons.title: Density Decides: Wood, Stone and Steel
lessons.focus: Average density vs water (1000 kg/m³) predicts floating; the steel nail sinks but the steel sufuria floats — shape matters.
lessons.advanced: A hollow steel ball's average density is 600 kg/m³: what fraction of its volume is air?

lessons.title: Upthrust: Water Pushes Back
lessons.focus: Weigh a stone in air, then in water: apparent weight drops; upthrust measured with a spring balance.
lessons.advanced: Stone: 2.5 N in air, 1.5 N in water: upthrust, displaced water weight, and the stone's volume.

lessons.title: Archimedes' Principle
lessons.focus: Upthrust equals weight of displaced fluid; verify by collecting overflow from the eureka can and weighing it.
lessons.advanced: Show a floating object's displaced weight equals its own weight — derive the floating condition.

lessons.title: The Eureka Can Lab: Volume by Overflow
lessons.focus: Measure irregular volumes precisely by overflow; link displacement to Unit 1 density measurements.
lessons.advanced: An object displaces 120 mL and weighs 3.0 N in air: density, and will it float?

lessons.title: Why Ships Float: Shape Beats Material
lessons.focus: Same clay ball sinks, same clay as a bowl floats; average density includes the hollow; dhow and ferry examples.
lessons.advanced: Compute the minimum hollow fraction for a steel hull (ρ=7800) to float; why do ships sink when swamped?

lessons.title: Clay Boat Challenge I: Design for Cargo
lessons.focus: Design a clay hull to carry bottle-top cargo; predict capacity from displaced volume.
lessons.advanced: Boat clay mass 200 g; hull displaces 800 cm³ at gunwale: maximum safe cargo in grams?

lessons.title: Clay Boat Challenge II: Load Test and Stability
lessons.focus: Load to sinking; record capacity; stability: wide beams vs tall cargo; freeboard concept.
lessons.advanced: Explain via centre of gravity vs centre of buoyancy why top-heavy boats capsize.

lessons.title: The Hydrometer: A Floater That Measures
lessons.focus: Floating depth reveals density; milk purity testing at the dairy; battery acid testers; salinity for fish farmers.
lessons.advanced: Why does the hydrometer sink deeper in less-dense liquid? Derive the depth-density relation for a uniform stick.

lessons.title: Build: A Pencil Hydrometer
lessons.focus: Weight a pencil with clay, float it, mark fresh-water line, calibrate with salt solutions; test unknowns.
lessons.advanced: Calibrate marks at 1.00, 1.05, 1.10 g/cm³: describe how you verified each.

lessons.title: Layers of Liquid: The Egg in Salt Water
lessons.focus: Egg sinks in fresh, floats in strong salt solution; density columns (salty below fresh, carefully poured).
lessons.advanced: Compute the salt concentration needed for neutral buoyancy of an egg (ρ≈1.05 g/cm³) — method and caveats.

lessons.title: Submarines and Swim Bladders
lessons.focus: Fish adjust a gas bladder; submarines flood and blow ballast tanks; Cartesian diver (Unit 7) as the working model.
lessons.advanced: A submarine at constant depth takes on water: what must happen to its ballast and why?

lessons.title: Rafts, Canoes and Ferries of Kenya
lessons.focus: Banana-stem and ambatch rafts, dugout canoes on Lake Victoria, ferries at Likoni; buoyancy calculations for safe loading.
lessons.advanced: Raft of 10 logs, each 40 L displacement, total mass 150 kg: safe passenger load in kg?

lessons.title: Life Jackets and Water Safety
lessons.focus: How a life jacket adds buoyancy without adding weight; cold water and panic; community water-safety campaign design.
lessons.advanced: A 70 kg person (body density ≈ 1.02) needs how much extra displaced volume to float face-up? Show working.

lessons.title: Plimsoll Lines: Loading Marks on Ships
lessons.focus: Load lines for fresh vs salt water; mark your clay boat's Plimsoll line; overloading tragedies discussion.
lessons.advanced: A ship moves from sea (1.025) to fresh water (1.000): by what percentage does displaced volume change?

lessons.title: Hot Air Rises: Buoyancy in Gases
lessons.focus: Smoke rises; teacher demo tissue hot-air balloon; air has density too; bridge to thermal physics (Unit on temperature in CBE 1.4).
lessons.advanced: Hot air at 0.9 kg/m³ in a 1 m³ balloon, outside 1.2: net lift force in newtons; payload in grams.

lessons.title: Design Project: A Floating Garden or Fish Cage
lessons.focus: Design a buoyant platform for vegetables (jerricans under bamboo); compute buoyancy budget; present.
lessons.advanced: Full buoyancy budget: platform + soil + water + crop vs total displacement, with 30% safety margin.

lessons.title: Unit Review: Regatta Day
lessons.focus: Clay-boat races, hydrometer readings, buoyancy puzzle stations; unit quiz.
lessons.advanced: Championship problem: design a boat to carry 500 g in salt water with minimal clay — show the displacement math.
